51303595.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to recombinant PPARgamma (unknown origin) by isothermal titration calorimetry

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Isothermal Titra: Isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) was conducted on an Affinity ITC (TA Instruments Affinity ITC). The recombinant PPARγ ligand binding domain protein (180–250 μM) or the RXRα ligand binding domain protein (110–230 μM) and the corresponding Wy14,643 derivatives (20–40 μM) were each dissolved in N-(2-hydroxyethyl)piperazine-N'-ethanesulfonic acid buffer (25 mM; adjusted to pH 7.5 with KOH; further containing 150 mM KF, 10% glycerol (w/w), 1% DMSO (v/v) and 5 mM dithiothreitol). The ITC instrument was adjusted to a temperature of 25 °C and the stirring rate was set at 75 rpm. 190 μL compound solution was filled into the reaction cell and PPARγ/RXRα ligand binding domain solution was titrated in 19–25 injections. The first injection had a reduced volume of 1.0 μL and was followed by injections of 2.5 μL. An interval of 300 s was maintained between individual injections. The heat of dilution resulting from titrating PPARγ/RXRα ligand binding domain protein solution into the buffer solution was recorded in an additional ITC run and subtracted from the raw ITC data obtained for the Wy14,643 derivatives. ITC raw data were analyzed using a NanoAnalyze software package (version 3.7.5). An independent binding model was used to fit the reaction enthalpy (ΔH), binding affinity constant (Kd), and stoichiometry (n). Free energy change (ΔG) was calculated from the equation ΔG = –RT ln K and the entropy (ΔS) was calculated from ΔG = ΔH – TΔS.

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 25 mM N-(2-hydroxyethyl)piperazine-N'-ethanesulfonic acid, 150 mM KF, 10% glycerol (w/w), 1% DMSO (v/v), 5 mM dithiothreitol

original_paragraph.Results section - ITC data: To exclude unspecific effects and confirm the activity of 2, 7, 20, 27, and 28 on RXRs and PPARs, we studied their interaction with the recombinant ligand binding domains of RXRα and PPARγ by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC, Table 2 and Figures S1–S10)37 and observed Kd values in agreement with the EC50s retrieved in the cellular assays. Minor mismatches between Kd and EC50 may arise from cellular effects in the reporter gene assay such as cellular uptake or degradation. The ITC experiments especially confirmed high affinity of 28 to RXRα with a double-digit nanomolar Kd value. Compared to the free diarylamine 27, 28 gained almost a factor 10 in affinity towards RXRs. According to our molecular docking studies (Figure 2c,d) this seems due to favorable binding of the methyl group in a lipophilic sub-pocket close to helix 11 that is not explored by either co-crystallized rexinoid. We also observed binding of 28 to PPARγ but the reporter gene assays revealed that the compound fails to cause appreciable PPARγ activation. Molecular docking of 28 in the PPARγ ligand binding domain (Figure S11a) suggested that its bulky trifluoromethyl substituent and N-methyl residue force 28 to a binding mode in the PPARγ ligand binding domain that prevents the formation of canonical H-bond contacts with the activation triad His323, Tyr327, and His449 resulting in failure to activate the nuclear receptor. Similar observations also hold true for PPARα (Figure S11b).

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 25 mM N-(2-hydroxyethyl)piperazine-N'-ethanesulfonic acid, 150 mM KF, 10% glycerol (w/w), 1% DMSO (v/v), 5 mM dithiothreitol

The ITC instrument was adjusted to a temperature of 25 °C and the stirring rate was set at 75 rpm. 190 μL compound solution was filled into the reaction cell and PPARγ or RXRα ligand binding domain solution was titrated in 19–25 injections. The first injection had a reduced volume of 1.0 μL and was followed by injections of 2.5 μL. An interval of 300 s was maintained between individual injections. The heat of dilution resulting from titrating PPARγ/RXRα ligand binding domain protein solution into the buffer solution was recorded in an additional ITC run and subtracted from the raw ITC data obtained for the Wy14,643 derivatives. ITC raw data were analyzed using a NanoAnalyze software package (version 3.7.5). An independent binding model was used to fit the reaction enthalpy (ΔH), binding affinity constant (Kd), and stoichiometry (n). Free energy change (ΔG) was calculated from the equation ΔG = –RT ln K and the entropy (ΔS) was calculated from ΔG = ΔH – TΔS.

original_paragraph.Results section - ITC data: To exclude unspecific effects and confirm the activity of 2, 7, 20, 27, and 28 on RXRs and PPARs, we studied their interaction with the recombinant ligand binding domains of RXRα and PPARγ by isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC, Table 2 and Figures S1–S10)37 and observed Kd values in agreement with the EC50s retrieved in the cellular assays. Minor mismatches between Kd and EC50 may arise from cellular effects in the reporter gene assay such as cellular uptake or degradation. The ITC experiments especially confirmed high affinity of 28 to RXRα with a double-digit nanomolar Kd value. Compared to the free diarylamine 27, 28 gained almost a factor 10 in affinity towards RXRs. According to our molecular docking studies (Figure 2c,d) this seems due to favorable binding of the methyl group in a lipophilic sub-pocket close to helix 11 that is not explored by either co-crystallized rexinoid. We also observed binding of 28 to PPARγ but the reporter gene assays revealed that the compound fails to cause appreciable PPARγ activation. Molecular docking of 28 in the PPARγ ligand binding domain (Figure S11a) suggested that its bulky trifluoromethyl substituent and N-methyl residue force 28 to a binding mode in the PPARγ ligand binding domain that prevents the formation of canonical H-bond contacts with the activation triad His323, Tyr327, and His449 resulting in failure to activate the nuclear receptor. Similar observations also hold true for PPARα (Figure S11b).

assay_conditions.buffer_composition: 25 mM N-(2-hydroxyethyl)piperazine-N'-ethanesulfonic acid, 150 mM KF, 10% glycerol (w/w), 1% DMSO (v/v), 5 mM dithiothreitol
